prompt:
I need the front end for Shelfwright. An in-house merchandising tool at a national home-improvement retailer that controls how each product category behaves on the company's website and app.

Who's using it: Kevin Osterberg, a senior online merchandiser in the e-commerce department who owns the Outdoor Power Equipment category. He's comfortable with the tool's rules but needs approval from his manager for anything affecting more than 500 products.

What they're doing right now: Ahead of the post-Thanksgiving snow-blower push, Kevin is reconfiguring the 'Snow Blowers' subcategory. He wants to change the default sort from 'best selling' to 'in stock near you first', promote two battery-powered brands for the next 3 weeks, choose which product attributes shoppers can narrow by and in what order, and decide whether out-of-stock items get hidden or pushed to the end. Before it goes live, he needs to compare his changes against the current settings and schedule them.

What's in the system at this point: Subcategory 'Snow Blowers': 412 active products (138 single-stage, 201 two-stage, 47 three-stage, 26 electric/battery), 7 brands. Current rules: default sort best-selling, 2 brand boosts expired Nov 1, out-of-stock items shown with a notice, 9 shopper-narrowing attributes (clearing width, stage, power source, start type, brand, price, rating, drive type, chute control). Proposed: boost brands 'Voltaris' and 'Northpeak' Nov 27–Dec 18, add 'battery platform' as an attribute, hide out-of-stock items in regions with under 10% availability. Inventory snapshot: 61% of products in stock nationally, 22% in the Northeast. Change history: 14 prior edits, last by Kevin on Oct 30. Approver: Lisa Cheng, Director of Seasonal.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
